reviews.title: tokoroten replayability 5-play threshold and Shikhondo one-sentence core tension
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex game work can still stack mechanics, evaluation layers, and replay-depth assumptions before naming how many plays a normal player or validation route is expected to survive. The transferable point is narrow: separate run-1 core readability from optional depth that only emerges after several repeats, and avoid treating designer-depth as player-facing evidence. Existing probes cover runtime integration, traces, composition depth, and style adherence, but not the assumed replayability budget that determines whether deeper layers are reachable. Keep this reversible and scoped to playable prototypes and game evaluation notes.
probe: Before the next playable prototype, game README or design note, headless/browser evaluation, or game acceptance note, did I name the expected replayability budget N, such as one run, three attempts, five attempts, or practice-heavy, instead of assuming infinite designer replay?
Did I separate the run-1 core experience from optional depth that requires N+1 or repeated mastery, such as combo layers, resource loops, hidden scoring, advanced movement, or late-stage strategy?

If a mechanic, acceptance criterion, or memory claim depends on repeated play, did I mark whether the evidence is within_budget, optional_depth, replayability_unverified, or designer_depth_only before using it to justify added complexity?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two playable-prototype or game-evaluation notes already name expected replayability budget N, separate run-1 core from optional repeat-play depth, and label repeated-play assumptions before adding mechanics or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible replayability-budget probe: name expected play-count N, separate first-run core from optional repeat-play depth, and label mechanics that rely on repeated play before accepting added complexity.

reviews.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
reviews.reason: Score 17. Existing anti-bloat checks say to avoid permanent rules, and the recent load-strategy probe scopes context loading, but neither asks for a held-out validation case or a rejected-edit memory before changing directive-like text. Keep this as a reversible instruction-edit validation probe, not an automated SkillOpt loop or broad mandate to edit AGENTS.
probe: Before the next directive, AGENTS, phase prompt, skill, reusable checklist, or self-feedback probe edit, did I name one held-out validation case, past failure, known counterexample, or task class the edit must not regress instead of relying only on the current example?
Did I classify the proposed text change as add, delete, or replace, and keep the learning rate small by limiting it to one behavioral target with an explicit scope and withdrawal condition?
If the edit is not adopted or validation is weak, did I record the rejected direction and reason in state, staging, or a local note so the same tempting rule expansion is not rediscovered next cycle?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two directive, AGENTS, phase prompt, skill, checklist, or self-feedback-probe edits already name a held-out validation case or counterexample, keep the edit to one scoped behavior change, and record rejected directions when validation is weak.

change.summary: Added a reversible SkillOpt-inspired instruction-edit validation probe: require a held-out case or counterexample, classify add/delete/replace with small edit scope, and record rejected rule directions before durable instruction-like edits.

The shared-read reframes the question from whether an agent sounds human or helpful to whether its role-conditioned answer should be trusted. Existing probes cover tool trajectory, verifier multiplicity, and memory recall failures, but they do not require a lightweight trust-signal split before accepting a smooth answer. Keep this as a reversible probe rather than adding a permanent safety rule.
probe: Before the next Slack post, memory update, shared-reads analysis, game-evaluation note, or agent-assisted code task where I rely on an LLM or agent answer, did I separate fluent/helpful style from evidence that the answer is trustworthy?

If the answer is self-serving, unusually smooth, source-light, role-conditioned, or conflicts with local files/logs, did I run one small adversarial or consistency check such as source lookup, diff/log comparison, alternate phrasing, or constraint question before accepting it?
If I cannot verify the trust signal, did I label the output as draft/untrusted and avoid basing a Slack post, memory directive, game judgment, or irreversible repo action solely on that answer?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two Slack posts, memory updates, shared-reads analyses, game-evaluation notes, or agent-assisted code tasks that rely on LLM/agent output already separate fluency from trust evidence and label unverifiable answers as draft or untrusted before action.

reviews.title: EGOSTREAM: streaming episodic memory benchmark for egocentric agents
reviews.reason: Score 16. This shared-read is useful now because Codex memory work, phase handoffs, and game-agent evaluations can treat a recall miss as simply forgotten even when the cause is state change, missing observation, compression loss, temporal-window mismatch, or identity/topic collision. EGOSTREAM frames continuous episodic memory as a diagnostic problem over what is remembered, over what time span, and as what information type. Existing lifecycle and safety probes name memory phases and touched surfaces, but they do not require a failure-mode split for streaming or episodic recall claims. Keep this as a reversible probe rather than a permanent memory rule.
probe: Before the next memory recall, session_context use, phase handoff, game-agent evaluation, or episodic-memory note where I report a remembered/missed item, did I classify the main recall claim by time span and information type instead of only saying found or forgotten?

If recall fails or conflicts, did I distinguish Forgotten/Not stored, State changed, Observation missing, Compression or summary loss, Temporal-window mismatch, Identity or topic collision, and Unknown before changing memory format, prompts, or evaluation criteria?

If the cause is Unknown, did I name one minimal evidence check such as source_ts lookup, raw log reread, atom excerpt comparison, staging diff, or replay marker before treating the failure as a memory-system defect?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory recall, session_context, phase handoff, game-agent evaluation, or episodic-memory notes already classify recall failures by time span, information type, and failure cause before proposing fixes.

reviews.title: SeClaw: execution-trajectory security evaluation for autonomous agents
reviews.reason: Score 15. This shared-read is useful now because Codex phase work touches local files, memory state, tools, browser/dev servers, git, and sometimes Slack/API surfaces, while existing safety practice mostly checks final outputs or pre-command intent. SeClaw reframes autonomous-agent safety around the trajectory: which tool, file, memory, or external service was touched, and where an unsafe action was approached. Existing repo rules already prohibit destructive or secret-bearing operations, so this should remain a reversible trajectory-awareness probe rather than a permanent rule or new harness.
probe: Before the next file-editing, memory-writing, Slack/API, browser-automation, dev-server, git, or external-service task where I report completion, did I name the touched surface: tool, file path, memory record, service, credential boundary, or repo state?

If the task approaches a sensitive action such as delete, overwrite, push, Slack post, external API call, secret-bearing file, plugin/skill install, or broad filesystem traversal, did I record the safety boundary and the evidence that kept the action within scope?

If the final output is safe but the trajectory included a near-miss, blocked command, unexpected file/service touch, or ambiguous instruction, did I classify it as tool misuse, file/memory exposure, privilege boundary, external-service risk, prompt/instruction ambiguity, or unknown before changing the workflow?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two file-editing, memory-writing, Slack/API, browser-automation, dev-server, git, or external-service tasks already record touched surfaces and classify any sensitive near-miss before claiming completion.

reviews.title: SWE-Marathon: long-horizon coding agents need multi-layer verification and failure taxonomy
reviews.reason: Score 17. This shared-read is useful now because Codex phase work and game playable diffs can still stop at a single visible success signal such as file changed, test passed, Slack posted, or screenshot exists. SWE-Marathon frames long-horizon agent work as both horizon difficulty and verifier-strength difficulty, and its failure taxonomy distinguishes implementation failure, timeout, reward hacking, premature termination, and poor self-verification. Existing probes cover many specialized evaluator boundaries, but they do not require a lightweight multi-signal completion check before declaring a long-running phase or playable diff done. Keep this as a reversible probe rather than adding a permanent phase gate.
probe: Before the next long-running phase task, playable diff, shared-reads posting run, or agent-assisted code task where I declare done, did I name at least two independent verifier signals instead of relying on one visible pass?

If the task fails or stalls, did I classify the dominant failure as Implementation Failure, Timeout, Reward Hacking, Premature Termination, Poor Self-Verification, or Unknown before changing prompts, code, phase gates, or tests?
If only one verifier signal is feasible, did I label the completion claim as narrow and name the missing verifier signal rather than treating the task as broadly complete?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two long-running phase tasks, playable diffs, shared-reads posting runs, or agent-assisted code tasks already record multiple verifier signals and classify failures before remediation.

reviews.title: ARC-AGI-3 interactive benchmark: exploration / modeling / goal-setting failure split
reviews.reason: Score 16. This shared-read is useful now because Codex game-agent and headless evaluation notes can collapse several different failures into a generic not playable or agent failed verdict. ARC-AGI-3 frames interactive puzzle solving as distinct capabilities such as exploration, world modeling, goal-setting, and solving under sparse observations. Existing probes separate agent-facing input surfaces, progress detectors, and fixed-persona coverage, but they do not require a lightweight failure-layer label before changing the game or the evaluator. Keep this as a reversible probe for the next game-agent or interactive benchmark note rather than adding a new benchmark framework.
probe: Before the next game-agent, headless replay, browser playtest, or interactive benchmark evaluation where I report success or failure, did I classify the main bottleneck as Exploration, Modeling, Goal-Setting, Execution/Control, Observation/Progress detection, or Unknown?

If the agent was not given an explicit goal or win condition, did I avoid calling the failure a bad policy until I record evidence about whether it explored enough, inferred mechanics, or identified a plausible goal?

If the layer is Unknown, did I name one minimal discriminating run, marker, or log field that would separate exploration failure from modeling or goal-setting failure before changing game rules, prompts, or harness code?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game-agent, headless replay, browser playtest, or interactive benchmark notes already classify failures by exploration, modeling, goal-setting, execution/control, and observation/progress detection before proposing fixes.

reviews.title: Playtesting: What is Beyond Personas
reviews.reason: Score 16. This shared-read is useful now because Codex game-agent or headless playtest work can over-trust fixed archetypal personas such as collector, killer, or exit seeker. The atom points to playtesting beyond static personas: agents may change objective mid-run, avoid a previously used solution, or trade off goals after state changes. Existing probes separate agent-facing surfaces and situation generation, but they do not ask whether a persona-passing run is merely a fixed-goal route. Keep this as a reversible probe for the next game-agent or automated playtest note rather than adding a new playtesting framework.
probe: Before the next game-agent, headless playtest, browser playtest, persona-based simulation, or automated level evaluation, did I state whether the agent objective is fixed for the whole run or can change with state, risk, discovery, or prior route knowledge?

If a fixed persona passes, did I avoid treating that as broad player coverage until I test or name one non-fixed behavior such as switching goals mid-run, avoiding a previously solved route, abandoning a risky reward, or seeking new information?
If I cannot test dynamic behavior, did I label the result as fixed-persona coverage and name the missing state-conditioned behavior instead of claiming human-like or general playability evidence?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game-agent or automated playtest notes already distinguish fixed-persona coverage from state-conditioned or route-aware behavior before claiming broad playability.

reviews.title: AGENTCL: memory transfer gain over recall success
reviews.reason: Score 17. The shared-read is useful now because Phase 3b can otherwise treat reading and adopting a probe as success, even when the remembered item does not improve the next phase output, Slack post, or playable diff. AGENTCL reframes memory evaluation from retrieval success to controlled task stream transfer gain. Existing read-to-action probes already require an evidence pointer, so I did not add another active probe. The small change is to evaluate the next memory-influenced output by whether the recalled atom changed a downstream artifact, reduced a repeat failure, or was explicitly marked read-only.

metric.name: recall_to_transfer_gain
metric.check: For the next memory-influenced Phase 3b, Phase 4, shared-reads analysis, or game-design output, record one downstream artifact or skipped-action reason showing whether the recalled atom changed the output rather than only being retrievable.

reviews.withdrawal_condition: Retire this metric if the next two memory-influenced phase notes already record downstream artifact evidence or read-only status without extra prompting.

reviews.title: VideoGameBench: raw screen / action / progress detector split for playable-diff evaluation
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Nao_u_BOT game work can accidentally prove that a prototype is readable only through debug state, internal JSON, or human-only overlays. VideoGameBench separates raw frame and legal action from checkpoint/progress detection and Lite latency controls, which maps directly to Codex playable-diff verification. Existing probes cover structural/semantic validity, clean/corruption GUI checks, and checkable intermediate state, but they do not require naming the agent-facing input surface separately from CI/human debug evidence before claiming playability or agent readability. Keep this as a reversible evaluation-surface probe rather than adding a new benchmark framework.
probe: Before the next playable diff, browser-game verification, headless replay, or game-agent evaluation where I claim readability, playability, or progress, did I name the agent-facing input surface separately from debug or CI-only evidence?

Did I record at least one progress detector or checkpoint type, such as raw-screen/UI match, deterministic internal state, event/log marker, or human-visible screenshot/clip, and state which one supports the claim?

If I use internal state, overlays, semantic actions, paused emulation, or extra tools, did I label the run as scaffolded/CI-facing instead of raw-agent-facing, and avoid using it as proof that the game can be understood from the player screen alone?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two playable-diff, browser-game verification, headless replay, or game-agent evaluation notes already separate agent-facing input surface from CI/human debug evidence and name the progress detector before claiming readability or playability.

reviews.title: akari_worlds「忘却=エントロピー散逸」が B033（非随意的忘却=エントロピック損失）に物理学的外部裏付けを与えた
reviews.reason: Score 15. This atom is useful now because Codex Phase 4 and shared-reads cleanup can treat forgetting, pruning, or compression as a free cleanup action after usage-signal and lifecycle checks pass. The shared-read frames forgetting as an active irreversible operation with asymmetric reconstruction cost, while also warning that Landauer equivalence is only a bounded analogy. Existing probes already require usage signals, lifecycle phase, trigger class, and mechanism boundaries, so the only non-redundant addition is a narrow reversible cost probe: before removing or compressing an active memory surface, name what future reconstruction would cost and the cheaper alternative.
probe: Before the next memory cleanup, compression, archive, supersede, pruning, or active-surface reduction that would make information harder to retrieve, did I name the likely reconstruction cost: extra recall/search time, source re-read, lost context, duplicate Slack/thread work, or missed game-design cue?

Did I compare that cost with one cheaper alternative such as keep hot, demote to cold index, add backlink, summarize with source_ts, expire later, or leave unchanged until an external usage signal appears?
If the cost and alternative are only metaphorical or unmeasured, did I downgrade the Landauer/B033 framing to an analogy and avoid claiming quantitative entropy or physical equivalence?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory cleanup, compression, archive, supersede, pruning, or active-surface-reduction notes already name reconstruction cost, compare a lower-cost alternative, and avoid quantitative entropy claims without measurement.

reviews.title: 5/24 メモリ系3論文横断 — 字段明示化 vs 既存温度値の再解釈 (Log視点)
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex memory work keeps facing the temptation to add schema fields such as stability, decay_hint, or conflict_with when an existing score, timestamp, validation note, or human-operated conflict record may already approximate the needed judgment. Existing probes cover memory lifecycle, 3-axis description, governance gates, and overwrite-versus-grounded updates, but they do not require a trial period where candidate judgment vocabulary proves it changes recall or integration decisions before becoming a persistent field. Keep this as a reversible field-promotion probe rather than adding SSGM-style fields to atoms.
probe: Before the next memory schema, atom/index field, recall-output label, or memory_redesign change, did I name the candidate judgment word and the existing signal that may already approximate it, such as score, source_ts, validation deadline, lifecycle status, related/conflict note, or human feedback log?

Did I test the word first in recall or staging output and record one concrete decision it changed, such as deprioritize, verify-before-use, link-as-conflict, keep-as-hypothesis, or promote-to-action, before making it a persistent field?
If no concrete decision changes, did I keep the idea as local vocabulary and avoid adding schema, index, directive, or AGENTS/phase-prompt text?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory schema, recall-output, atom/index-field, or memory_redesign notes already compare candidate fields against existing signals and show a decision change before promotion.

reviews.title: Draw2Think: Propose-Draw-Verify loop with engine-checkable intermediate state
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Phase 3b and game-memory work can still leave intermediate reasoning as natural-language notes that are plausible but not checkable. Draw2Think reframes the improvement as moving the next step through a typed action, external state, and verifier feedback loop. Existing probes separate structural/semantic validity and outcome evidence, but they do not require Codex to name the intermediate state that can actually be inspected before the next action. Keep this as a reversible probe for the next memory, evaluation, or playable-diff step rather than a new validator framework.
probe: Before the next memory, evaluation, playable-diff, level/puzzle, or harness change where I claim progress from reasoning or generated content, did I name the checkable intermediate state, such as JSON state, board/canvas state, dependency graph, log trace, metric row, or staging artifact?
Did I separate the proposed action from the verifier feedback: what operation changed the state, what constraint or observation accepted/rejected it, and what measurement or failure reason came back?
If the intermediate state is only prose or a subjective impression, did I downgrade the claim to hypothesis and name the smallest external check or artifact needed before using it as evidence?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory/evaluation/playable-diff notes already name a checkable intermediate state and separate proposed action from verifier feedback before claiming progress.

reviews.title: Online Agent-as-a-Judge: Situation-Generating Evaluation for Interactive Agents
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex can judge NPC, tutorial, social-interaction, or memory-continuity behavior from whatever log happens to exist, even when the critical conflict, support request, promise follow-through, or role-consistency situation never occurred. Existing probes cover proxy boundaries, structural/semantic validity, and clean versus corrupted GUI runs, but they do not require evidence acquisition before scoring an interactive/social criterion. Keep this as a reversible situation-generation probe rather than a new benchmark or permanent judge workflow.
probe: Before the next NPC, social interaction, tutorial dialogue, support character, memory-continuity, or interactive-agent evaluation, did I name the designer criterion and the missing situation that an ordinary passive log may not contain?

Did I state whether the criterion should be judged by a deterministic outcome metric first, or by a generated situation trace because the target behavior is social, contextual, or otherwise non-endpoint?

If I use a judge NPC, probe script, or staged interaction, did I keep hidden-state inspection read-only and separate induced dialogue evidence from follow-through action evidence before giving pass, fail, or insufficient?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two NPC/social-interaction, tutorial-dialogue, support-character, memory-continuity, or interactive-agent evaluation notes already name the missing situation and separate outcome metrics, generated trace evidence, and follow-through action evidence before scoring.

reviews.title: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex memory work can name lifecycle phases while still leaving the memory unit under-specified: whether it is episodic or semantic, text/file/graph-like, and manually controlled or policy-driven. The shared-read and follow-up discussion point to temporal scope, representational substrate, and control policy, with Nao_u-side guidance to borrow the structure without adding a new automation device. Existing probes cover lifecycle phase and admission, but not this compact 3-axis description before changing memory/state structures.
probe: Before the next memory/state structure change, recall-index edit, atom promotion, compression note, or memory-tree consolidation step, did I name the memory unit on three axes: temporal scope, representational substrate, and control policy?

If I propose a new field, index, directive, or lifecycle change, did I state whether it changes what is stored, how it is represented, or when it is written/read/merged/forgotten, instead of treating all memory improvement as one action?
Did I keep this as descriptive structure first and avoid adding automation, thresholds, or persistent rules unless a concrete failure trace requires them?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory/state structure or recall-index notes already describe temporal scope, representational substrate, and control policy before changing fields, indices, directives, or lifecycle behavior.

reviews.title: Memory lifecycle phase responsibility split for Write/Retrieve/Execute-Share/Forget
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex phase work can confuse a retrieval failure, write-format problem, execution/share handoff problem, and forget/compression decision as one generic memory issue. The shared-read gives a narrow reversible framing: classify the lifecycle phase before changing memory tools, staging, recall, or Slack/shared surfaces. Existing probes cover trigger classes, admission control, and control-plane boundaries, but they do not require lifecycle-phase responsibility to be named before diagnosing a memory-cycle issue.
probe: Before the next memory, recall, compression, staging, shared-reads, Slack handoff, or phase-maintenance action, did I name the lifecycle phase being touched: Write, Store, Retrieve, Execute/Share, or Forget/Compress?

If a failure or improvement is claimed, did I classify it in that phase instead of mixing retrieval misses, write-format gaps, execution/share handoff friction, and retention/forget decisions into one generic memory problem?
If the work crosses phase boundaries or another instance would consume it, did I state the handoff artifact and one adjacent-phase counterexample that would show the boundary is wrong or too slow?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory, recall, compression, staging, shared-reads, Slack handoff, or phase-maintenance notes already classify lifecycle phase and adjacent handoff risk before changing tools or persistent state.

reviews.title: Difficulty Curve-Based Procedural Generation of Scrolling Shooter Enemy Formations
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because STG enemy placement and verify.js-style checks can reduce balance to a single pass/fail or a hand-waved difficulty feeling, while the shared-read gives a narrow reversible framing: compare an intended difficulty curve with observed danger_over_time, then keep player fun/readiness outside that proxy. Existing DDA and local/global probes cover proxy boundaries and generator layers, but they do not require Codex to name the source of an ideal curve and the observed danger trace before claiming a wave or formation is balanced.
probe: Before the next STG enemy wave, formation, spawn table, scrolling segment, or balance verification, did I name the intended difficulty curve or proxy source before changing placement values?

Did I record at least one observed danger_over_time signal or surrogate trace, such as enemy density, bullet pressure, death-nearby spike, survival window, or route pressure, before claiming the formation is balanced?
If I use an ideal curve, did I state whether it came from explicit Nao_u input, an existing graze_log/template, or my own hypothesis, and keep fun/readiness claims separate from RMSE or curve fit?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two STG enemy-wave, formation, spawn-table, scrolling-segment, or balance-verification notes already separate intended difficulty curve source from observed danger trace before claiming balance.

reviews.title: GamePlot: LLM-powered assistant for game plot design with play-through revision
reviews.reason: Score 16. This atom is useful now because Codex can too easily treat LLM narrative output as a text artifact, while GamePlot frames narrative design as an editable design room plus a game room where turns are played and revised. Existing probes cover scoped generation, local/global evaluator splits, and player-facing meaning, but they do not require a proposed story, dialogue, branch, or NPC beat to be traced as playable turn/state evidence before calling it a design improvement. Keep this as a reversible narrative-playthrough probe, not a permanent narrative workflow.
probe: Before the next narrative, NPC, dialogue, quest, branch, tutorial text, or story-facing game prototype change, did I separate the design-room artifact from the game-room evidence: authored premise/instruction/examples versus a playable turn sequence, state change, or player-choice trace?
If an LLM generates or revises story content, did I test at least one concrete player action or branch against the generated beat before claiming the narrative improved?
If the result only reads well as text, did I keep it as draft material and name the missing playable evidence, such as choice consequence, UI cue, NPC response, pacing beat, or state transition?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two narrative, NPC, dialogue, quest, branch, tutorial-text, or story-facing prototype notes already separate authored design artifacts from playable turn/state evidence before claiming narrative improvement.

reviews.title: AgentHijack: GUI agent robustness under common environment corruptions
reviews.reason: Score 16. This atom is useful now because browser-use, Playwright, and GUI-agent checks can make a clean successful run look stronger than it is. Existing probes already require real input and a small playable rubric, but they do not ask whether viewport, focus, overlay, delayed input, or load disturbance can break the same interaction. Keep this as a reversible corruption probe for the next browser game or GUI verification, not a full AgentHijack benchmark or a broad robustness requirement.
probe: Before the next browser game playable diff, browser-use check, Playwright verification, or GUI-agent playtest, did I separate the clean interaction path from at least one small corruption path such as viewport or DPR change, focus loss, overlay, delayed input, or load delay?
If the clean path passes, did I avoid upgrading the claim to robust/playable until I state which corruption was not tested and why it is outside this pass?

If a corruption probe fails, did I classify the failure as environment robustness, UI layout/focus handling, automation fragility, or game interaction design before changing code or judging the game feel?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two browser game or GUI-agent verification notes already separate clean interaction success from small environment-corruption checks before claiming playability or robustness.

reviews.title: AI game implementation flag pile-up x diegetic UI
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because AI-assisted game implementation can accumulate isolated flags that satisfy local requests while hiding the actual game-state model from the player. Existing probes cover route contracts, local/global generator layers, difficulty proxies, and behavior slices, but they do not ask whether a new boolean or branch should be expressed as world state, player-facing feedback, or diegetic presentation. Keep this as a reversible implementation probe for the next game prototype diff, not a general ban on flags.
probe: Before the next game prototype diff, scripted event, UI cue, enemy behavior, combo/graze mechanic, or progression change, did I name whether each new condition is a transient implementation flag, durable world state, player-facing feedback, or diegetic presentation?

If I add a boolean, branch, cooldown, unlock, or mode variable, did I ask whether the player can infer it from world objects, animation, sound, spatial relation, risk/reward pressure, or UI state instead of only from hidden logic?

If a flag is kept hidden, did I state why it is purely technical and name one regression or trace that would reveal flag pile-up, such as contradictory states, duplicated branches, unreadable feedback, or a stale event trigger?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game prototype diffs or game-state design notes already classify new conditions as implementation flag, world state, player feedback, or diegetic presentation before adding branches.

reviews.title: Stuck in the Middle: Generating Levels without (or with) Softlocks
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because level, route, and mission generation can pass a start-to-goal solvability check while still creating reachable mid-run states that cannot recover after optional exploration, resource use, or path deviation. Existing probes cover task compatibility, local/global evaluator split, BDD route contracts, and objective-environment solvability, but they do not require Codex to distinguish a single solution path from recoverability across reachable intermediate states. Keep this as a reversible softlock probe for the next level/map/mission generation or route validation note, not a permanent generator constraint.
probe: Before the next level, map, route, mission, puzzle, resource-placement, or traversal-generation task, did I check more than one start-to-goal solution path and name at least one reachable mid-state or off-path state that must still be recoverable?

If a route succeeds, did I avoid calling the content safe until I considered softlock risks from optional branches, one-way movement, consumable resources, timing windows, enemy/object state changes, or player deviation from the intended path?

If recoverability is uncertain, did I keep the result as a candidate and name the smallest deterministic check, scripted detour, reachability query, or manual trace needed before promoting it as playable content?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two level/map/route/mission/puzzle or traversal-generation notes already separate start-to-goal solvability from recoverability of reachable intermediate/off-path states before claiming playability.

reviews.title: SLM x agentic networks for dynamic game content generation
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because future game prototypes and agentic PCG work can too easily ask one broad LLM/agent to generate, judge, and explain content, then mistake retry success for local quality. The shared-read narrows the useful claim to scoped subtasks, constrained output structure, retry-until-success, and a separate judge gate, while explicitly preserving local quality assessment as an open problem. Existing probes cover local/global evaluator splits and overconfidence, but they do not require Codex to define the generation subtask boundary and judge acceptance condition before relying on retry loops. Keep this as a reversible one-cycle probe, not an SLM implementation requirement.
probe: Before the next narrative, level, encounter, dialogue, mission, enemy-pattern, or other game-content generation task, did I name the narrow subtask boundary and constrained output structure before asking an LLM or agent to generate?

If I use retry-until-success, critique, judge, or repair, did I define the judge acceptance condition separately from the generator and avoid treating pass/fail as proof of local fun, style, or player quality?
If local quality is still unclear, did I keep the result as a candidate and name the missing measurement or human judgment instead of promoting it as validated content?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game-content generation or agentic-PCG notes already name scoped subtasks, constrained output structure, separate judge gates, and the remaining local-quality uncertainty before claiming validation.

reviews.title: Adaptive Memory Admission Control for LLM Agents
reviews.reason: Score 16. This atom is useful now because Phase 3b, memory ingest, candidate promotion, and game-lesson writes all create persistent memory before any later forgetting or cleanup mechanism can help. The shared-read separates write-time admission from retention/forgetting and names five interpretable factors: future utility, factual reliability, semantic novelty, recency, and content-type prior. Existing probes cover stale premises, concrete evidence anchors, local/global generation failures, and forgetting signals, but they do not require Codex to name why a new memory item deserves admission at write time. Keep this as a reversible one-cycle admission probe, not a new memory_admission_check.py requirement.
probe: Before the next memory atom, candidate promotion, project memory note, game lesson, or lasting directive/probe write, did I name which admission reason applies: future utility, factual reliability, semantic novelty, recency, or content-type prior?
If the reason is content-type prior, did I state why this type deserves stricter or looser admission than routine logs, drafts, candidates, feedback rules, project notes, or shared-reads?
If no admission reason can be named, did I keep the item as raw/staging/candidate material instead of promoting it to persistent memory or a directive?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two persistent memory or directive writes already state a write-time admission reason, or if it starts causing useful raw evidence to be discarded instead of staged.

reviews.title: Learning Local Constraints for Reinforcement-Learned Content Generators
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex game work and Phase 0 playable diffs often generate levels, waves, or enemy placements and then judge failures as one undifferentiated quality problem. The shared-read separates local pattern constraints from global playability rewards and shows that input diversity, rare-pattern pruning, and proxy rewards can pull in different directions. Existing probes cover PCGML representation/repair, task compatibility, DDA proxy boundaries, and route contracts, but they do not require Codex to classify generation failures by local constraints, global evaluator, or input/action-space design before changing the generator. Keep this as a reversible generation-layer probe, not a WCRL implementation requirement.
probe: Before the next level, wave, enemy-placement, map, reward-placement, or functional content generation task, did I name the local constraints separately from the global evaluator, such as adjacency or placement rules versus reachability, completion, route time, score, collection, or headless trace metrics?

If the generated content fails, did I classify the failure layer before editing: local constraint violation, global evaluator failure, proxy/reward mismatch, input corpus/action-space too narrow, input corpus/action-space too diverse, or missing bridge/intermediate pattern?

If I add diversity, prune rare patterns, change rewards, or widen the generator action space, did I name one counter-signal to watch, such as contradictions, impossible routes, solvable-but-ugly output, natural-but-unsolvable output, or proxy-passing content that is boring or strategically flat?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two level, wave, enemy-placement, map, reward-placement, or functional-content generation notes already separate local constraints from global evaluators and classify failures by layer before generator changes.

reviews.title: (arxiv 2602.03315, 2026-02) / Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
reviews.reason: Score 16. reviews.reason: Score 17. reviews.title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
reviews.reason: In Nao_u_BOT memory_recall, shared-reads, and game-rights search, the practical risk is not only grep versus vector. It is whether results are delivered inline or as file paths, and whether the agent closes the read-integrate-retry loop. This overlaps with existing memory-layer probes, so it should stay as a reversible one-cycle probe for the next recall improvement, Phase 4a, or dedupe search.

reviews.title: ebikani_hasami「Agents need control flow, not more prompts」(HN 433pts) — 我々の5/2事件と3層プロンプト構造を「制御フロー」として読み直す
reviews.reason: 定時サイクルは既に長い指示群を持っており、次に改善すべきなのは文言追加ではなく、Phase間の順番・分岐・失敗時の扱いが実際に機能しているかの確認である。この atom は prompt 増量ではなく control flow として agent 運用を読むため、恒久ルール化せず、次回の phase handoff / tool failure / retry 判断で1回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: karaage0703「放牧エンジニアリング」と、自分の backup auto-commit が意図 commit を窒息させた事故の接続 (Ash)
reviews.reason: Git sync is mandatory after work, so mixing scheduler, ingest, or backup-generated changes into an intentional commit can pollute the evidence trail and make later recall or rollback decisions worse. This atom connects houboku-style autonomous operation with a backup auto-commit incident that suffocated the intended commit. Existing AGENTS.md already has the permanent rule, so this cycle only adds a short reversible probe for the next git sync.

reviews.title: MEMSAD 自分達の環境への適用: shared-reads/Slack/game-rights の記憶汚染リスク
reviews.reason: shared-reads と Slack 指示を atom 化して再利用する運用では、浅い要約・出所欠落・過剰一般化が長期記憶として残り、後続 recall の判断を歪める。既存の投稿品質ルールと重なるが、今回の反映は恒久ルールではなく、次回の recall / memory ingest / shared-reads state 更新で「検索されやすいが根拠が弱い記憶」を1回だけ点検する軽量 probe に留める。

reviews.title: multi-agent LLM の drift メトリクス 3 本が 2026-05 に独立収束 - Pot (Log/Mir/Ash/Nao_u) 構成への構造的接続
reviews.reason: この atom は multi-agent LLM の drift を意味的 drift、行動的 drift、artifact decay の 3 層に分け、Pot 構成では A は許容、B は抑制、C は強く抑制という暫定線引きを置いている。直近の Phase 3b probe は aggregate score や reviewer bias の分解には触れているが、Codex 自身の定時サイクルが core anchor、警告の経験化、artifact decay を同時に点検する短い問いはまだ薄い。恒久ルール化すると監視項目が肥大化するため、次の memory cleanup / multi-agent evaluation / phase handoff で 1 回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: Agent Island: A Saturation- and Contamination-Resistant Benchmark from Multiagent Games
reviews.reason: Agent Island は multiagent game log を leaderboard だけでなく、private note、public pitch、vote rationale、final decision、same-provider preference まで含む評価 artifact として残す点が、直近の game harness / cross_review / shared-reads 判断に直結する。ただし 2-4 agent 評価を恒久制度にすると重く、Cattle Trade の aggregate score 分解 probe とも一部重なるため、次に複数 agent / 複数レビューで prototype や候補を評価する 1 回だけ、最終結論だけでなく投票理由と同調 bias を保存する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: shmup 単調性回避の外部知見3本 — graze_log v04 (5/14 Nao_u指摘) への種として整理
reviews.reason: Nao_u の graze_log v04 指摘は「単調・単純」「軌跡予測がない」「shot_log のようなリズム/バリエーション必要」で、直近の shmup / action prototype の修復判断に直結する。ただし既に wave/rhythm probe は存在するため、恒久ルールや大きな評価表へ広げず、次回だけ「variation が学習可能な反復として効いているか、単なるランダム化や密度上げに逃げていないか」を見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Cattle Trade: multi-agent negotiation benchmark with incomplete information and resource constraints
reviews.reason: Cattle Trade frames agent evaluation as a long game where incomplete information, adversarial interaction, auctions, hidden offers, bluffing, opponent-state inference, and resource allocation interact. This is directly useful for game/agent evaluation, but turning it into a permanent rule would overreach. A one-cycle probe can keep the next benchmark or prototype judgment from collapsing success into a single score.

reviews.title: @DenneTA_D 「翻訳=非可逆圧縮」× @akari_worlds 「一語で起動するネットワーク」 — R-007 造語症対策の射程画定と、MEMORY.md / cross_review / 3インスタンス転送の理論的限界
reviews.reason: Phase 1/3b/4a can mistake a MEMORY.md index line, atom trigger, or staging summary for the original context. This atom shows that compression preserves propositions but can lose anchor tokens such as proper nouns, incident names, Slack timestamps, and source links. A permanent rule would make every recall heavier, so this is kept as a short probe for the next memory/staging/cross_review summary use.

reviews.title: GAM: Hierarchical Graph-based Agentic Memory for LLM Agents — 3層グラフ記憶 (arXiv 2604.12285v1)
reviews.reason: Phase 1/4a の記憶検索が grep や直近 atom 直引きに寄りやすく、上位目標から中粒度記憶、atom へ降りる順序が明示されていない。GAM の知見は現行 memory_redesign と per-file atoms に直結するが、MEMORY.md 再設計や検索プロトコル恒久化は大きすぎるため、次の memory recall / Phase 4a で1回だけ階層検索順序を試す probe に留める。

reviews.title: Eneba「15 Best Shoot 'Em Up Games to Try In 2026」分析 — Phase 1 §6 仮設の自己訂正
reviews.reason: 直近の shot_log / shmup 評価で、flow state や反射操作を単独の成功軸として読みすぎる危険を、商業評価語彙の分布と BOMB headless ベンチの方向一致で訂正している。恒久ルール化すると二次情報を過大評価するため、次の game prototype / repair の前に「戦術判断」と「反射操作」を分けて確認する一時 probe に留める。

reviews.title: 2026-05-16 Twitter おすすめから3件結合: creatable / fun / sellable の三独立軸
reviews.reason: 直近のゲーム制作では、作れること、面白いこと、売れることを混同すると、headless や実装進捗を fun 軸の進捗として誤読しやすい。この atom は mTsuruta / hadekait / snapwith の3観察を creatable / fun / sellable の独立軸として結合し、graze_log v05 の headless と fun 判定の混同にも直接接続している。恒久ルールや AGENTS 追記にはせず、次に game prototype の制作・評価・修復を行う時だけ、軸混同を確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: LLM Game Rule Understanding Through Out-of-Distribution Fine-Tuning
reviews.reason: ゲームプロトタイプを LLM に読ませる前に、感想や改造案へ飛ばず、明示ルールを状態遷移へ適用できているかを測る必要がある。この atom は legal 判定と next state 判定を分け、ID/OOD split と回答理由で失敗原因を分類する設計が、次の rule-understanding harness に直接使える。恒久ルールや評価表にはせず、次に仕様レビュー・turn/grid/resource 系 prototype を扱う時の短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: PCGRLLM: LLM を reward/probe 候補生成と具体 feedback に使い、score oracle にしない
reviews.reason: 直近のゲーム制作では、面白さや制作意図を deterministic harness に落とす必要がある。PCGRLLM は LLM を評価器ではなく reward/probe の生成・修正補助に置き、生成物からの具体 feedback を1点ずつ返す構造が直接使える。恒久ルールや評価表にはせず、次に PCG / レベル生成 / playtest probe を設計する時の短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Lanzi/Loiacono: LLMをinteractive genetic algorithmの操作子として使う共同ゲーム設計
reviews.reason: 次のゲーム制作で「候補を大量に作る」だけに戻らず、人間や過去feedbackの選択圧を明示してから小さく変異・交叉する手順へ落とせる。恒久ルール化せず、次回のゲーム案選定で1回だけ確認するprobeに留める。

reviews.title: trajectory 二重使用 — エージェント記憶設計と弾幕物理軌跡が同じ語を別意味で使う構造
reviews.reason: Fang et al. の trajectory から tips を抽出する構造と、graze_log 側の物理軌跡を知覚補助へ変換する構造は、直近の記憶整理とゲーム制作の両方に接続する。ただし原典確認は二次情報経由で confidence medium のため、記憶スキーマや恒久ルールには昇格せず、次の staging / game prototype / memory cleanup で「結果だけでなく決定帰属つき trajectory から 1 つだけ再利用可能な tip を抜く」短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [shared-reads] devwhodevs/engraph: 5 レーン RRF ハイブリッド検索で markdown vault をエージェント記憶基盤にする MCP/REST server
reviews.reason: 現行の memory_recall / grep / per-file atom 運用に対し、engraph の要点は多機能導入ではなく「semantic / full-text / graph / rerank / time の複数レーンを read-only で比べ、どのレーンが効いたかを説明可能にしてから Write を開ける」こと。記憶基盤を恒久変更せず、次の recall 設計や Phase 4a 整理で 1 回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: 「人間は判断だけ」と「判断は厚みで成り立つ」の反証ペア — M-40 自己判定ハーネスを二層に分ける根拠
reviews.reason: 自己判定を headless 数値だけに寄せる既存 probe はあるが、この atom は「機械的に判定できる層」と「自分の基準の厚みが必要な層」を事前に分ける点が未反映。次のゲーム評価で、どちらを自動化し、どちらを判断保留または人間確認へ残すかを明示する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: 速度ヒューリスティックと事前批判の3層切り分け（ktch9541 / Mark Brown / toRisouP / xiombatsg）
reviews.reason: 多案 harness、単一案着手前、実装中の論法を分ける視点は、次のゲーム案選定で速度足切りと事前批判を混同しないために直接使える。既存ルールへ追記せず、次回の案選定・着手判断で層を1行確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] When Routine Chats Turn Toxic: Unintended Long-Term State Poisoning in Personalized Agents
reviews.reason: 長期状態への書き戻しが確認境界・tool default・自律範囲を静かに変える問題が、現在の memory / directive / phase 改善サイクルに直結するため。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] VeRO: An Evaluation Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
reviews.reason: agent-as-code の改善を内面の自己評価ではなく edit-execute-evaluate の外部 harness として扱う視点が、現在のゲーム制作サイクルの「記憶整理・ルール解釈だけで成果扱いになる」失敗に直結するため。

reviews.title: M-40「人間プレイ依存からの脱却 — 自己判定ハーネス」と外部研究3件の三角化観察 — kaizen #106 自発外部検索の収穫
reviews.reason: Nao_u の「人間のプレイに依存せず、ちゃんと自分で判断できるようになって」という指示は重要だが、直近では不完全なヘッドレス観測を設計判断に使う失敗も出ているため、自己判定の前に測定装置の成立を確認する小さな probe として反映する。

reviews.title: 弾幕系敵生成の業界実装は3経路に収束している——graze_log v05 hybrid 化の根拠
reviews.reason: 直近サイクルが game balancing / playtesting / MMO simulation を扱い、graze_log v05 hybrid 化の根拠にも接続するため。恒久ルール化せず、次のゲーム設計時に「手作り/完全生成/hybrid のどれを選んだか」と「検証可能な最小 harness があるか」だけを見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] RuleSmith: Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Game Balancing
reviews.reason: 直近 Phase 1/2 が game balancing と LLM/game evaluation を扱っており、RuleSmith の「LLM を審査員ではなく候補比較 harness の一部として使う」視点が、次の小規模ゲーム調整で具体行動に落としやすいため。恒久ルールではなく、候補ルールを同一 harness で比較する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review
reviews.reason: Memory / Skills / Protocols / Harness Engineering の境界整理は、Phase 3b が避けたい恒久ルール肥大化を直接抑える。既存の記憶・directive・skill更新判断に、昇格前の短い確認として差し込めるため、恒久ルールではなく可逆な probe に留める。

reviews.title: Automated Playtesting with Procedural Personas through MCTS with Evolved Heuristics
reviews.reason: 単一の上手い bot では見えない設計上の偏りを、複数 persona の行動差として測る知見が、次の game prototype / headless 評価に直接効くため。MCTS 完全実装ではなく、軽量 persona と同一ログ比較に絞れば小さく試せる。

reviews.title: R_Nikaido 5/13「自分で気付けた感」= Insight Design (MIT 2015 学術ジャンル既存) — 5/8 Linelith Rule Discovery の隣に立つ第3軸
reviews.reason: 知識アンロックや発見感を、説明の追加ではなくプレイヤーが自力で結び付けたと感じる経路として設計する視点が、次の game prototype / game-design 評価に直接効くため。恒久ルール化せず、次回1回の設計確認に絞れば可逆に試せる。

reviews.title: Codex Symphony の失敗→ハーネス更新ループは「見える失敗」しか拾えない——窒息装置の沈黙バグ問題
reviews.reason: ハーネス更新ループが「見える失敗」だけを学習信号にする盲点は、定時サイクルの成功判定や game prototype 検証で無出力・未実行・検出不能を見逃す問題に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回の検証設計で沈黙する失敗条件を1つ確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: @plu_plus 「『こう作るべき』より『ここで迷った／気持ちよかった』」を、本日 12:09 に自分が出した cross_review と強制照合した
reviews.reason: headless 計測や設計批評の説得力に乗って、観察ではなく処方を渡してしまう失敗は、次の game prototype / cross_review / self-feedback に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回レビューで観察と処方の比率だけを見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: ebikani_hasami「sandbox-first bug reproduction」を我々の backup auto-commit 先回り事件と合成。intent isolation の workflow 層が空いていたことの言語化
reviews.reason: bugfix 前の disposable sandbox と production tree 非接触という骨子は、Codex 定時サイクルで Slack投稿・記憶更新・git同期など異なる intent を同じ作業面で混ぜてしまうリスクに直結するため。恒久ルールではなく、次回のファイル変更や検証設計で intent の隔離境界を確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] The PokeAgent Challenge: Competitive and Long-Context Learning at Scale
reviews.reason: Pokemon benchmark 自体ではなく、model / harness / 観測 / milestone / 失敗復帰を分けて記録する発想が、次の game prototype headless 評価や自動プレイログ設計に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回評価ログで milestone と観測制限を分けて残す短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] SAGE: Semantic-Aware Gray-Box Game Regression Testing with Large Language Models
reviews.reason: SAGE is useful here because it treats regression testing as update-aware test selection, not full-suite execution. Full RL/graph implementation is too heavy for the current small game cycle, but mapping change tags to existing headless checks or playtest routes is small, reversible, and directly actionable.

reviews.title: Grounding Machine Creativity in Game Design Knowledge Representations
reviews.reason: ゲーム制作指示を直接コードへ流さず、goal pattern / intermediate spec / replay / grounding-hygiene taxonomy に分ける視点が、次の playable diff と失敗記録に直結する。既存の rule-understanding や reward/probe 系と近いが、今回は実装前の薄い中間仕様と失敗分類に限定すれば重複と肥大化を避けられるため、恒久ルールではなく短期 probe として採用する。

reviews.title: Boghog's bullet hell shmup 101 — shmups.wiki digital library
reviews.reason: 弾幕 wave design を、敵生成位置・タイミング・レーン・重畳のような検証可能な規則へ落とす知見。次回ゲーム制作で「動くが単調」になりやすい敵/障害物配置を、抽象ルールではなく小さな spawn-pattern probe として確認できる。既存の恒久ルールとは重複させず、次の playable diff で1回だけ使う短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: @kuina_ch x @akari_worlds - natural-language test runner as the other party
reviews.reason: Game self-judgment, cross_review, and Slack/shared-reads effectiveness checks can confuse internally closed headless/self checks with verdicts that only exist after another party responds. This overlaps with existing M-40 and headless cautions, but a one-cycle check for who the runner is remains small, reversible, and does not add a permanent rule.

reviews.title: AutoUE: making 3D game generation an engine-verifiable production pipeline
reviews.reason: AutoUE is Unreal-specific, but its useful lesson is to split production into engine-grounded asset/layout, rule-module, interactive object, and runtime-test slices. Recent game work can conflate visuals, code completion, interaction, and headless runtime evidence, so this is adopted only as a reversible probe for the next playable diff.

reviews.title: @AI_masaou「HTML vs Markdown」議論を、人間が読まない領域はAIの目標ドリフト未検知領域になる、という軸に再定義した投稿
reviews.reason: 今回のPhase 3でPowerShell stdin経由の投稿が文字化けし、stagingにも読みにくいログが残っている。shared-readsやstagingは人間が読めて初めて介入余地になるため、恒久ルール追加ではなく、次の投稿・staging・commit説明で「読み手が介入できる形か」を1回確認する軽いprobeに留める。

reviews.title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games ? VLM???????Codex ??????????shot_log vs graze_log?????????
遊星歯車機関（千葉集）「正解に三つの鐘が鳴る ― プレイヤーを名探偵にするメカニクスについて」 (note, 2026-05-22 Nao_u 共有)
reviews.reason: Nao_u 共有の ADV/ミステリ設計資料で、答え合わせを即時二値にすると推理余地が消え、最後に一括すると総当たりになるという問題を、段階的確証・近さの表示・未発見手がかりでほどく知見。直近の playable diff と headless 評価は合否や到達率へ寄りやすいため、次回のゲーム評価で「部分的に正しい試行をどう見せ、総当たりをどう防ぐか」を1回だけ確認する probe にする。既存の headless 差分 probe と隣接するので恒久ルール化しない。

reviews.title: #game-rights 3連投メタプロンプト「ゲーム制作で LLM がデフォルトでは落としがちなこと」への Log 評価
reviews.reason: Pulse Relay 固有の教師差分を 8 観点へ圧縮した投稿で、直近の v006/v007 系 playable diff に直結する。既存のゲーム設計ルールへ恒久追記すると肥大化するため、次のゲーム実装・評価で「中心入力」「特殊システム3状態」「bad policy headless」を物理化できたかだけを見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Shared-reads 6-post series: Pulse Relay v003 supervised delta packet for autonomous game creation (1/6-6/6)
reviews.reason: Unreviewed score-18 atom spanning memory, harness, game-design, agent, operation, and evaluation. Existing game_design_rules 12/13 and the center-input probe already cover the implementation gate, so this cycle adds only a reversible probe for the non-compression boundary: do not flatten user fixes or teacher deltas into short improvement labels before preserving raw signal, mismatch, failed judgment, and the next implementation gate. The referenced lesson files are missing in this worktree, so adoption is bounded to the atom excerpt and existing index/rule links.

reviews.title: Agentic PCG: Procedural Content Generation via Tool-using LLMs
reviews.reason: Agentic PCG は、LLM を一発生成器ではなく、環境を観察し、計画し、既存の PCG/編集/評価ツールを呼び、結果を修正する循環として扱う点が、次のゲーム制作や headless 評価に直結する。既存の fixed-test vs dynamic stress や lab-proxy probe と重なる部分はあるため、恒久ルールや評価表にはせず、PCG/レベル生成/ゲーム素材生成の場面で tool loop と評価根拠を確認する可逆 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Ash @KAKUBOMB「SteamでAI量産15パズルが組織的に絨毯爆撃→跳ねるべき」(2026-05-10)
reviews.reason: AI量産品が市場や審査で同型テンプレートとして扱われる観察は、次のゲーム制作で「動く」「生成できた」「既存ジャンルに似ている」を成果判定にしてしまう危険に直結する。既存の lab-proxy / Q0 / prior-art probes と隣接するが、市場・審査・他者の選別目線で artifact と actor/spam-filter を分ける観点は未レビューで有用。恒久ルールではなく、次の game prototype / shared-reads 候補 / self_judgment で1回だけ、量産テンプレートから跳ねる理由を確認する可逆 probe に留める。

reviews.title: RuleSmith: Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Game Balancing
